_note: Landowner big game permit programs by state, researched 2026-09-21 from state statutes, rules and agency pages. 'sell' is what the state's own text allows: yes / direct (landowner to hunter only, no broker) / no / silent. Not legal advice. Re-check every spring; several states had bills moving.

states.name: Utah
states.program: Three separate programs. Landowner Association permits (rule R657-43) for limited-entry deer, elk and pronghorn units where landowners hold more than half the private land. CWMU permits (R657-37) on private ranches of 5,000 to 10,000+ acres. Mitigation permits and vouchers (R657-44) for documented crop or fence damage.
states.sell_plain: Landowner Association vouchers may be sold: the rule says a landowner receiving one "may sell or otherwise transfer such Voucher to any legal hunter" with a Utah hunting license. General-season private-land-only buck deer vouchers may also be sold. Unit-wide buck deer vouchers may only go to immediate family. CWMU vouchers are designated under the rules, not sold on an open market. Mitigation permits are tied to the damaged property and are not sellable.
states.broker: Not addressed in the rules. Anyone paid $100 or more to help a hunter on public land must hold a DWR guide or outfitter registration (SB149, in force July 2025).
states.price: Not published. Broker listings seen around $6,500 for a deer voucher (secondary source).
states.depredation: Mitigation permits and vouchers under R657-44 go to landowners with a DWR-approved damage plan; the landowner designates the hunter (family or employee). Not sellable.
states.access: Walk-In Access program: free annual authorization number, wildlife.utah.gov/walkinaccess.
states.cite: Utah Admin. Rules R657-43, R657-37, R657-44; wildlife.utah.gov/rules. R657-43 last amended June 2026.
states.changed: 2026 amendments to R657-43 and R657-37; watch the RAC packets.

states.name: Colorado
states.program: Landowner Preference Program: agricultural parcels of 160 acres or more with deer, elk or pronghorn get vouchers for limited licenses in that unit.
states.sell_plain: A landowner may transfer a voucher, for money, directly to the hunter who will use it. The rule: vouchers "shall only be transferred by the landowner or the landowner's land manager, if any, directly to an individual." And: "No person shall broker a voucher on behalf of any landowner or person, or use or possess any brokered voucher." A brokered voucher and the licence bought with it are void.
states.price: Roughly $1,500 to $6,000 reported on forums and land-company sites (secondary).
states.depredation: Game Damage Program pays for damage; landowners in it may not unreasonably restrict hunting and may charge no more than $500 per person per season for access. Whether damage permits can be transferred was not found in the rule text.
states.access: Walk-In Access program, about 166,000 acres, foot access only: cpw.state.co.us.

states.name: New Mexico
states.program: E-PLUS (Elk Private Land Use System): ranches with elk get elk authorizations by zone - Primary (acreage formula), Special (negotiated), Secondary (self-registered, unlimited). Elk only; deer and pronghorn use separate private-land licences.
states.sell_plain: The department's own page: authorizations "can then be bartered, sold, or traded to hunters ... Any arrangements between hunters and landowners for elk authorizations or hunting leases are a private matter." The codified rule regulates only transfer between ranches in the same unit (with written landowner permission); sale is left to private arrangement.
states.broker: Not addressed anywhere in the rule; brokers and outfitters operate openly in the gap.
states.price: Not published. Outfitter listings about $6,000 to $8,000 for a bull elk authorization (secondary).
states.depredation: Depredation is a kill-on-complaint process under 19.30.2 NMAC; no compensation, no tag to sell, and those involved may not keep or bid on the animal.
states.access: Open Gate program, 19.34.7 NMAC, funded by the habitat stamp: wildlife.dgf.nm.gov.
states.changed: Species harvest rules were opened for comment in early 2026; E-PLUS rule itself not reopened.

states.name: Nevada
states.program: Deer and pronghorn damage compensation tags (one tag per 50 animals on the private land) and special incentive elk tags by agreement with the department.
states.sell_plain: Statute: a damage compensation tag "may be sold by that person to any holder of a valid Nevada hunting license at any price mutually agreed upon," for use on the private land or its unit. Elk incentive tags may likewise be sold "at any price upon which the parties mutually agree."
states.broker: Not addressed in statute or regulation; brokers operate openly.
states.price: Set by the parties. A forum figure of $20,000 or more for elk tags in units 76-81 (secondary, unverified).
states.depredation: Separate depredation kill permits (NAC 503.710-740): the animal is state property and may not be used by the permittee - nothing to sell.
states.access: No standalone paid-access program found; elk-incentive landowners must give reasonable access to adjoining public land where theirs is the only way in.
states.changed: NRS 502.145 last amended 2017; nothing pending found.

states.name: Wyoming
states.program: Landowner licences (Commission Chapter 44, section 8): deeded land of 160+ contiguous acres used by the species for 2,000 animal-days a year; up to two licences per species per parcel, for the landowner or immediate family. Separately, a $16 landowner coupon is paid whenever any hunter kills a deer, elk or pronghorn on the deeded land.
states.sell_plain: The licence can only be applied for and used by the landowner or immediate family, so there is nothing to sell. The coupon is explicit: "Landowner's coupons are not transferable. Any unauthorized person attempting to collect any sum for any landowner's coupon is guilty of a high misdemeanor." In February 2026 the Senate rejected a bill to allow open-market sale of landowner tags, 6 to 25.
states.price: None lawful. Landowners charge for access instead (a reported $500 a deer near Devils Tower, secondary).
states.depredation: Damage claims are paid from a state fund (W.S. 23-1-901); auxiliary management hunts issue permits to public hunters, not landowners.
states.access: Access Yes: walk-in hunting areas and hunter management areas (permission slip). wgfd.wyo.gov/public-access.
states.cite: W.S. 23-1-302(h); W.S. 23-3-105 (coupons); Commission Chapter 44 section 8 (July 2026 text).
states.changed: 2025 proposal to raise the acreage threshold withdrawn; 2026 sale bill (SF 51) and cap bills failed.

states.name: Idaho
states.program: Landowner Appreciation Program: controlled-hunt tags drawn by acreage lottery for eligible property of 640+ acres (320-639 acres only for leftovers) in one game management unit; deer, elk, pronghorn, black bear (turkey in the rule).
states.sell_plain: The rule: "It is unlawful for anyone other than the Department ... to sell or market LAP controlled hunt tags, and it is unlawful for a person to buy an LAP controlled hunt tag from any person other than the Department." Three-year program ban on top of any penalty. The landowner may designate one eligible person to receive the tag.
states.price: Application fee only: $6.25 resident, $18 nonresident per species. No lawful resale.
states.depredation: Landowner Permission Hunts (permission slip from a landowner of 160+ acres) and the damage compensation program under Idaho Code 36-1108 to 1110; no transferable tag.
states.access: Access Yes! pays landowners for public access: idfg.idaho.gov/yes.
states.cite: IDAPA 13.01.04 section 400 (in force July 1 2026); IDFG 2026 LAP brochure.
states.changed: Technical clean-up effective July 2026; the sale ban unchanged.

states.name: Montana
states.program: Landowner preference for deer and pronghorn on 160+ agricultural acres; landowner-sponsored nonresident combination licences (B-10 / B-11) on 640+ acres; supplemental game damage licences.
states.sell_plain: The sponsor must "accept no monetary consideration" for enabling a licence, and for damage licences "a landowner may not charge a fee to a hunter." Preference may be designated only to immediate family, an employed land manager, or a person with a developmental disability.
states.depredation: Supplemental game damage licences for antlerless animals; landowner designates the recipient; nontransferable; no fee to the hunter.
states.access: Block Management: free public access on about 6.8 million acres; landowners paid up to $17 a hunter-day. fwp.mt.gov.
states.changed: Legislature meets in odd years; nothing pending found for 2026.

states.name: Arizona
states.program: None. All big game tags go through the draw. House Bill 2147 (2026) would have created non-transferable landowner deer permits; it passed the House and died in the Senate.
states.sell_plain: There is no landowner tag to sell.
states.depredation: Handled by the department through special hunts, not landowner permits.
states.access: Landowner Relations Program and ranch-pass compacts in some units.

states.name: Oregon
states.program: Landowner Preference Program: 40+ contiguous acres for deer and western elk; 160+ for eastern buck deer, bull elk and pronghorn. Tags are for the landowner and immediate family.
states.sell_plain: Tags are for landowners and immediate family. The rule allows exchanging a tag for another "for no charge"; it contains no provision for selling one to another person.
states.depredation: Landowner Damage Program: antlerless elk damage tags for documented damage; up to five per property; the rule is silent on sale.
states.access: Access and Habitat program, 2.6 million acres: myodfw.com.

states.name: California
states.program: Private Lands Management (PLM): ranches with an approved habitat plan get their own tags and seasons.
states.sell_plain: The rule is silent on selling the tag itself. In practice the licensee distributes the tags to hunters of their choosing and sells the hunt package; the tag is issued in the hunter's name and is valid only on that ranch.
states.price: State tag fee about $105; ranch packages $2,500 to $6,600 (outfitter listings, secondary).
states.depredation: Depredation permits are separate under the Fish and Game Code; not researched.
states.access: SHARE program: drawn access permits to private and landlocked land, wildlife.ca.gov/SHARE.
states.changed: Possible commission activity in 2026; not confirmed.

states.name: Washington
states.program: Landowner Hunting Permits by contract with the department; damage prevention permit hunts.
states.sell_plain: The rule: "Landowners may sell access associated with the landowner portion of the permits, but then must waive the right to all claims for wildlife damage that may occur on their lands." The permit goes with the access. In Elk Area 3721, access tied to damage permits may not be sold.
states.depredation: Damage prevention permits under a cooperative agreement; the landowner hands the permit to the hunter and gives up damage claims above a threshold.
states.access: Private Lands Access Program: Feel Free to Hunt, Register to Hunt, Hunt by Written Permission, Hunt by Reservation. wdfw.wa.gov.

states.name: Kansas
states.program: Hunt-Own-Land deer permits for landowners and tenants of 80+ acres; one per 80 acres.
states.sell_plain: Permits may be transferred to lineal or collateral relatives and their spouses; nonresident landowner permits are not transferable. No sale is authorized. A pending bill (HB 2672) would create a transferable landowner appreciation permit that "may not be sold."
states.price: Permit fees: nonresident tenant $85; special relative permit $42.50.
states.depredation: Deer damage control permits from the district biologist; landowner must allow firearm deer hunting on the land; not sellable.
states.access: Walk-In Hunting Access (WIHA), over a million acres: ksoutdoors.gov.
states.changed: SB 80 (2025-26) would end nonresident landowner permits; pending.

states.name: Nebraska
states.program: Landowner and leaseholder limited permits for deer, pronghorn, elk, turkey and (new) mountain lion on 80+ acres (320+ owned or 640+ leased for elk).
states.sell_plain: Permits are for the qualifying landowner or immediate family only. No transfer to others and no sale is provided for.
states.price: Not published in the sources read.
states.depredation: Damage control permits to a single landowner in the growing season; additional shooters can be added with the Commission; not sellable.
states.access: Open Fields and Waters: paid walk-in access on 471,000+ acres. outdoornebraska.gov.
states.changed: Application periods consolidated for 2025-26; mountain lion landowner permits added.

states.name: South Dakota
states.program: Landowner own-land deer and pronghorn licences; landowner preference in the drawings; nonresidents need 640+ contiguous acres west of the Missouri.
states.sell_plain: No transfer or sale provision was found; the licence is issued to the qualifying landowner personally. The official statute pages could not be opened directly, so this rests on a mirror.
states.price: Not published in the sources read.
states.depredation: Agency-run assistance (hazing, fencing, depredation hunts, stackyard cost-share); no transferable tag.
states.access: Walk-In Area program, 1.2 million acres: gfp.sd.gov.

states.name: Texas
states.program: Managed Lands Deer Program (MLDP): tags are issued to the landowner for the enrolled tract, not to individual hunters.
states.sell_plain: MLDP tags are valid only on the enrolled tract and are handed out by the landowner or agent. Texas landowners earn from hunting leases (access), not from selling the tag; the general ban on selling game (Parks and Wildlife Code 62.021) is the backdrop.
states.broker: Lease brokers are common; tag brokering is not addressed.
states.price: Enrollment $30 (Harvest Option) or $300 (Conservation Option); leases run higher on enrolled land.
states.access: Annual Public Hunting permit, $48, about 1.2 million acres including leased private land. tpwd.texas.gov.

states.name: Alaska
states.program: None. Less than one percent of the state is private land; tags come through drawings, registration and subsistence.
states.depredation: Defense of life or property lets anyone kill a threatening animal, with reporting; not a permit.
states.access: Not applicable - most land is public.

outfitter_note: Arranging or guiding a paid hunt is licensed work in most states. In Utah anyone paid $100 or more to assist a hunter on public land needs a DWR guide or outfitter registration (from July 2025). Colorado voids brokered vouchers. Treat any paid matching of hunters and landowners as needing a lawyer first.
